summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of gastroparesis, J-tube placement, and Nissen fundoplication was admitted for recurrent nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain, consistent with her prior flares. She had been discharged three days earlier but developed symptoms suddenly after eating a small amount of jello. In the ED, she was found to have hypokalemia, which was corrected with IV potassium. She was treated with IV fluids, bowel rest, and IV antiemetics including ondansetron, lorazepam, and prochlorperazine, with good symptom control. Her pain resolved overnight, and she advanced to oral intake. Labs remained stable, with no signs of infection or organ dysfunction. She was discharged home with instructions to use her J-tube for feeds, try oral ondansetron (Zofran) for breakthrough nausea, and follow up with her gastroenterologist. Home health services were arranged for J-tube support.
